doc.title: Hentoff Nat — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Sterling Brown and teaching jazz at Howard
summary: Hentoff praises Brown, who got jazz into Howard's curriculum by playing Stravinsky and Milhaud first.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: He was black, right? Howard University.

Sterling Brown was a black. So was Willard James. Sterling Brown was an expert on the blues, on black culture, on black history. He taught for a while at Howard University. He told me once that he was never allowed to teach jazz or blues as such, because in some of the black colleges – Billy Taylor talks about this too – they didn’t want jazz mentioned, because jazz had come out of these places, these brothels and gin mills, etc. So the way Sterling Brown got jazz into the curriculum at Howard, he would play [Igor] Stravinsky’s Ragtime or something by [Darius] Milhaud and say, “Now, I’ll show you where this came from.”
There’s a recording, just parenthetically, of Sterling Brown giving some introductions at the Sprituals to Swing concerts in ’39. They’re remarkable. They’re wonderful. They’re just . . .
Did you know him? Did you meet him?
Yeah. I met him, talked to him. I don’t think anybody has mentioned him in years.
Hardly. We’ll have to do something about that. Now we come to . . .
The Jazz Museum should have a section on Sterling Brown.
